facts.text: Upper Pohatcong’s name comes from the Lenni Lenape word Packatnsacunk, meaning “stream between split hills,” describing the valley carved by Pohatcong Creek.
Pohatcong Township, where Upper Pohatcong lies, was created in 1881 by the New Jersey General Assembly, taking land from Greenwich Township.
Before Europeans arrived, Lenni Lenape villages dotted the area, leaving jasper arrowheads, chert scrapers, and steatite hoes along Pohatcong Creek.
During the Revolutionary War, 60 Continental Army cavalry horses were wintered at a local sawmill in 1778, returning spring in excellent condition.
In the 19th and early 20th centuries, farmers in Upper Pohatcong powered mills on Pohatcong Creek to grind flour and process timber.
Upper Pohatcong sits in the northern part of Pohatcong Township, right next to the Delaware River that marks the New Jersey–Pennsylvania line.
